terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable 3D graphics terms. Avoid vague words unless they are paired with concrete geometry/material/shader parameters.

referenceCamera.note: For likeness work, solve the reference camera (forge/stage1_intake/solve_camera_pose.py) so the review render aligns with the photo and the reference can be projected. Confirm by overlay review.

objectClass.notes: Front orthographic studio view. Face outline measured as a rounded rectangle W=1032px H=1266px r=366px (r/W=0.355), fit verified at 3 independent rows. Handle is a surface of revolution. Only metal on the object is one gold collar ring.

reasoning: Silhouette is simple and analytically fittable (rounded rect + fillet + cylinder) — low silhouette score.
Six macro parts (face plate, edge guard, throat, collar, grip, butt cap) with a real parent-child join at the collar — moderate, not simple.
Two genuine repetition systems: the grip wrap helix and the grip perforation dot field.
Seven distinct material layers measured by median RGB, including one true metal.
Frontal-only view hides the entire Z axis (thickness, edge-guard bead depth, handle cross-section) — raises occlusion risk.
Intended for a web demo site: needs a swing pivot at the grip and a pickable/explodable hierarchy.

specDepthDecision.rationale: Observed structure has six macro parts, two repetition systems (wrap helix, perforation field) and localized surface overrides (perforation dots, edge-guard seam stipple). A macro-only spec would collapse the paddle into a flat plate on a stick and lose every identity feature. Repetition is present and real (the wrap helix, the perforation field) but neither is an instanced cluster: the helix is one swept component and the perforations are material channels. Recorded under observedRepetitions instead of repetitionSystems, which drives InstancedMesh emission.

detailInventory.note: Zones scanned from the component decomposition in analysis.md; grid-3x3 crops in ./zones retained as evidence. Every detail maps to a real component.localFeatures or material.localOverrides entry.

details.description: Face plate outline is a rounded rectangle with corner radius 366px over width 1032px (r/W=0.355). Predicted vs measured half-width agrees at y=141 (428/428.5), y=1101 (464/464), y=1165 (415/415.5).
Continuous bead running the full face perimeter, 12-18px wide inside the silhouette, standing proud of both face skins. Reads as a separate band, not a painted border.
Triangle mark with negative-space figure, plus 'PADDLE' (green, rgb 173/203/4), 'POWER' and 'PLAY. CONNECT. RECHARGE.' (cream). Matte ink, no sheen difference from the face field.
Single gold ring, median rgb 182/153/92, spanning y1410-1438. Value varies across its own width, which is the metal cue; the only metallic surface on the object.
Two near-black polymer rings (median rgb 26/29/33) flanking the gold ring: y1388-1408 above, y1440-1462 below.
Overwrap ridge running as a continuous helix down the grip barrel, ~11 turns over the 120mm grip length, each turn overlapping the last.
Sparse round perforations across the wrap. Measured dark-pixel fraction 0.036 of grip area — sparse dots, explicitly NOT a dense knurl or crosshatch.
Diagonal cut edge where the wrap terminates near the collar, visible as a short straight tonal break across the helix.
Grip barrel widens from 187px to 217px between y1900 and y2042 — a flared butt flange, same cream material family as the wrap.
Throat leaves the face plate's bottom corner arcs tangentially with no shoulder or step: widths at y1229 still sit on the fitted corner arc, y1293 and below depart from it.
Fine irregular stipple along the outermost edge-guard line, strongest along the upper perimeter. Micro roughness variation, not geometry.

anatomy.note: Only meaningful when objectClass.primaryDomain is character or hybrid. Set applies=true and fill from forge/stage1_intake/extract_landmarks.py. See grimoire/character/reconstruction.md and grimoire/character/likeness_maximization.md.

resolvedUnknowns: thickness-axis [undetermined-from-reference, needs a side/edge-on view]: total core thickness and edge-guard bead depth. Resolved from category convention (16 mm head, guard 2 mm proud per side) and flagged as inference, not measurement.
rear-face-graphic [hidden, needs a rear view]: whether the rear face carries the same decal. Assumed mirrored; many paddles print a different rear. Lowest-confidence visual claim (0.35).
handle-cross-section [undetermined-from-reference, needs a butt-end view]: round or octagonal core under the wrap. Modelled octagonal per category convention; the wrap hides it either way.
wrap-helix-pitch [uncertain, needs a grip close-up]: exact overwrap pitch and handedness. Estimated 11 right-handed turns over the 120 mm grip from low-contrast ridge spacing.
real-scale [not-derivable, needs a stated dimension]: true overall length. Set to 0.42 m from category convention; all other dimensions are measured pixel ratios, so proportions hold.
preSpecAssessment.resolvedUnknownsNote: All five were resolved by an explicitly labelled inference or convention rather than by new evidence. None blocks implementation; each is mirrored in spec.assumptions and each remains a reason to request the named extra view before treating the model as measured.

definitionOfDone: The rendered model matches the reference silhouette, primary proportions, visible component hierarchy, material response, and most recognizable local features for the selected fidelity tier.

featureGroups.name: Overall silhouette and proportions
qualityCriteria: Bounding shape, dominant curves, negative spaces, and scale relationships are explicitly described.
failureModes: model reads as a generic placeholder instead of the reference object
major proportions are guessed without evidence

featureGroups.name: Primary structure and hierarchy
qualityCriteria: Major parts, joints, seams, contact points, and parent-child relationships are named before code generation.
failureModes: large visible parts are merged into one mesh
component hierarchy is too shallow for the observed complexity

featureGroups.name: Attachment and joint correctness
qualityCriteria: Every visible child appendage, branch, limb, handle, connector, tube, cable, horn, wing, leg, or hinged part has an attachment contract with parent socket, localStart/localEnd, contact type, embed/overlap, and gap tolerance.
failureModes: child part root floats away from the parent
branch/limb/tube is centered in space instead of pivoting from its root
parent-child transform mixes world and local coordinates

featureGroups.name: Surface material response
qualityCriteria: Albedo zones, roughness, normal/bump/displacement intent, cavity dirt, edge wear, and local overrides are specified where visible.
Important materials define independent albedo, roughness, height/normal, and AO responses instead of reusing one texture for unrelated PBR channels.
Surface response is decomposed into macro, meso, and micro frequency bands with scale and amplitude tied to object scale.
failureModes: local material variation is missing or not tied to image evidence

featureGroups.name: Reference color, material, and lighting response
qualityCriteria: Material-pass names the reference-derived albedo palette, roughness variation, tactile normal/bump/displacement response, and local masks.
When a source image is available, run reference PBR extraction and require confidence >= 0.7 before treating maps as implementation-ready.
Lighting-pass names key/fill/rim or environment light, exposure, tone mapping, background, and contact shadow behavior.
Neutral, grazing-angle, and reference-matched renders prove that surface relief survives relighting and is not painted into albedo.
failureModes: model has acceptable shape but reads as flat shaded or plastic
colors are a generic average instead of reference-observed local color zones
lighting is evenly ambient and cannot reproduce the source value range

visualAcceptance.scoringRule: AI vision must inspect a side-by-side reference/render sheet and score the current pass from 0 to 1. Pixel-diff code may assist diagnostics but cannot approve a pass.

featureReviewPolicy.selectionRule: Choose only the most visually salient, identity-defining, user-prioritized, or high-risk semantic systems. Group repeated parts instead of reviewing every mesh. AI vision scores every selected feature from the same full reference/render pair.

screenshotPolicy.minimumEvidence: Each visual pass needs a reference image, rendered screenshot, side-by-side comparison sheet, AI vision score, layer scores, and critique before choosing continue.
screenshotPolicy.reviewPairRule: Compare the same camera/viewpoint whenever possible; do not judge a front reference against a random render angle.
screenshotPolicy.acceptanceAuthority: AI vision review of the comparison sheet. Code-generated pixel similarity is not sufficient evidence.

actionReadiness.contract: Every macro/meso component should be generated as a stable named Object3D pivot node with a mesh child, action metadata, optional sockets, collider proxy, and destruction metadata.
requiredComponentFields: attachment for child appendages, connectors, limbs, tubes, handles, legs, horns, wings, branches, or cables
authoringRules: Do not collapse independently movable parts into one mesh.
Put transforms on component pivot groups, not only on raw meshes.
For attached child parts, put the pivot at the semantic root/socket and build visible geometry from localStart to localEnd.
Represent hinge, socket, detachable, and breakable intent even when no animation is implemented yet.
Use simplified collider proxies for runtime physics instead of visual mesh colliders by default.

destructionPolicy.fractureGroupNaming: Use stable semantic names such as body-shell, left-hinge, glass-panel, branch-segment.
destructionPolicy.debrisStrategy: Prefer detachable component groups and a small number of procedural fragments over random mesh explosion.

assumptions: Overall length 0.42 m is category convention, not measured; all other dimensions are measured pixel ratios so proportions survive a wrong absolute scale.
Head thickness 0.0116 m with a 0.0160 m edge-guard bead is inferred from pickleball paddle convention. The frontal reference carries zero Z evidence.
The rear face mirrors the front graphic. Many paddles print a different rear; this is the lowest-confidence visual claim in the spec (0.35).
The handle core is octagonal under the wrap, per category convention. Never visible.

uv-remap-hand-refinement: ExtrudeGeometry emits UVs in local metres, so the generated factory's face plate UVs must be remapped to 0..1 over the profile bounding box before the de-lit albedo is applied. This is a documented post-generation code refinement, recorded here so the decision does not live only in generated code.
Wrap helix turn count (11) and handedness (right) are estimates from low-contrast ridge spacing.

authored-geometry-vs-attachment-cylinder: the generator substitutes a tapered cylinder along attachment.localStart -> localEnd for ANY component that has a complete attachment. That is right for the handle core and the three collar rings (they are cylinders, and their spans carry the measured radii), and wrong for the extruded face plate, the swept edge-guard bead, the two lathed grip parts and the tube helix, whose forms are authored in geometryDescriptor. A deterministic post-generation patch (tools/patch_paddle_factory.py) disables the substitution for those five and leaves their attachment metadata intact in userData. Re-run it after every regeneration; it is idempotent.

face-plate-uv-remap: the same patch rewrites the face plate's ExtrudeGeometry UVs from local metres to 0..1 over the profile bounding box, which is what lets the de-lit reference albedo land on the plate at the measured position instead of tiling.

coordinateFrame.front: +Z, the camera-facing striking skin in the reference

coordinateFrame.scaleReference: metres. Overall length 0.42 m set from category convention (not derivable from the image); every other dimension is a measured pixel ratio at S = 0.42 m / 2029 px.

componentTree.name: Paddle Power paddle (root)
componentTree.topologyRationale: Not a surface at all: a zero-scale, zero-opacity rig node that exists so the hierarchy has a single motion root with the swing pivot and sweet-spot sockets on it. It contributes no pixels, so it has no albedo to compare against the render.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: zero-scale rig root; carries no visible surface

sockets.notes: Hand/controller attach point; the swing pivot in the reference grip.
Ball contact point on the front face, at the face plate centroid.

collider.notes: Whole-object proxy for a swing arc.

surfaceDetail.normalPattern: reference-derived tangent normal from the de-lit crop

componentTree.name: Face plate
componentTree.topologyRationale: A constant-thickness composite panel with a flat front and back skin; its form is fully described by one measured 2D outline plus a depth, not by a sculpted volume.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: closed slab lofted from the measured 2D silhouette
geometryDescriptor.uvStrategy: planar-XY normalized to the profile bounding box; the generated extrude UVs are in local metres and MUST be remapped to 0..1 over the profile bbox before the de-lit face albedo is applied (see assumptions: uv-remap-hand-refinement)

sockets.notes: Front striking skin; carries the de-lit reference decal.
Rear skin; mirrored from the front (hidden in the reference).

collider.notes: Flat hit box over the striking face.

attachment.notes: Throat runs down into the collar; overlap is the collar embed depth.

surfaceDetail.normalPattern: fine irregular seam stipple along the outer line

componentTree.name: Perimeter edge guard
componentTree.topologyRationale: A flat band of constant width and thickness wrapping the face plate's rim. It conforms to the plate's outline rather than having a form of its own, and it is built as a ring in the same plane — not as a cross-section swept along a spine, which folded through itself.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: extruded ring: the measured outline, with an angle-bisector offset of the same outline as the hole, so the band keeps constant width through every corner
geometryDescriptor.uvStrategy: planar-XY; the guard carries no map, so UVs are not remapped

attachment.notes: Ring overlaps the face plate's outer 3.4 mm on both skins and stands 2.2 mm proud of each.

componentTree.name: Handle core
componentTree.topologyRationale: A straight turned shaft; a single revolved solid with no sculpted variation.

sockets.notes: Surface the overwrap is wound onto.
Distal end the butt cap seats into.

attachment.notes: Runs up inside the collar; fully hidden by wrap and collar in the reference.

componentTree.name: Collar ring — lower black
componentTree.topologyRationale: A discrete turned ring sitting on the shaft; a separate manufactured part.

attachment.notes: Ring seats around the shaft; span and radii are the measured ring band, expressed in the handle core's local frame.

componentTree.name: Collar ring — gold
componentTree.topologyRationale: A discrete turned metal ring; the only metal part, manufactured separately.

attachment.notes: Ring seats around the shaft; span and radii are the measured ring band, expressed in the handle core's local frame.

componentTree.name: Collar ring — upper black
componentTree.topologyRationale: A discrete turned ring sitting on the shaft; a separate manufactured part.

attachment.notes: Ring seats around the shaft; span and radii are the measured ring band, expressed in the handle core's local frame.

componentTree.name: Grip overwrap
componentTree.topologyRationale: A thin wrap that takes the shaft's form rather than having its own volume; its radius profile is measured off the silhouette, not sculpted.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: revolved shell over the shaft, tapering out into the collar
geometryDescriptor.uvStrategy: cylindrical (u around, v along the barrel)
geometryDescriptor.latheProfileEvidence: Radii read directly off mask rows y_img 1462/1470/1490/1520/1549/1600/1700/1800/1880/1900, converted at S = 0.42 m / 2029 px. Replaces the hand-smoothed first profile.

sockets.notes: Where a hand closes on the wrap.

attachment.notes: Wound directly onto the shaft; no gap.

surfaceDetail.normalPattern: same wrap grain as the host surface

componentTree.name: Overwrap ridge helix
componentTree.topologyRationale: A raised ridge riding on the wrap surface; relief on a host surface, not an independent volume.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: swept ridge following the overwrap helix

attachment.notes: Ridge sits on the wrap surface; rides with its parent when exploded.

componentTree.name: Butt cap
componentTree.topologyRationale: A separate moulded end piece with its own flared volume, seated on the shaft end rather than conforming to it.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: revolved flared flange closing the shaft end

attachment.notes: Seats over the shaft end; the flare is the measured 187 -> 217 px widening.

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Web demo prop: hold 60 fps on a mid laptop. Reach fidelity first, then cut segment counts on the helix and lathes — never the measured outline.

lightingFromPhoto: key: soft large source from the upper right; measured as a 10-level edge-guard value difference left vs right, and as the only directional cue in an otherwise flat frame
fill: broad and near-frontal — the face plate shows no falloff top to bottom
rim: none visible; the silhouette separates on background value, not on a rim highlight
background: pure white studio sweep, no cast shadow in frame
review renders must ALSO be captured under neutral light so material readability is judged independently of this reference lighting
exposure and tone mapping: ACES filmic at exposure 1.0 — the reference is a white-sweep product shot with no clipped highlight, so the render must not blow out the cream grip

contact shadow: a soft ground shadow under the butt cap when the paddle is staged upright; the reference frame has none, so it is a staging choice, and ambient occlusion carries the part-to-part darkening instead
proceduralStrategy: Block out the measured outline as one extruded slab plus a revolved handle; verify silhouette IoU first.
Add the collar ring stack, wrap, helix and butt cap as separate named pivot groups.
Sweep the edge-guard bead along the rim spine and check the cross-section does not twist off-axis.
Apply the de-lit reference albedo to the face plate with remapped planar UVs; keep roughness, height, normal and AO as independent channels.
Light with a key from the upper right plus broad frontal fill, then re-check under neutral light.
Cut helix and lathe segment counts last, and never the measured outline.
animationAnchors: root 'grip-hand' socket at y=0.070 is the swing pivot — a hand or controller attaches here
root 'sweet-spot' socket at the face centroid is the ball contact point for an impact response
facePlate 'face-front'/'face-back' sockets carry decals or hit decals without rebuilding geometry
every macro/meso part is its own named pivot group, so an exploded/assembly animation needs no rebuild
destructionAnchors: head-assembly (facePlate + edgeGuard) detaches from handle-assembly at the collar — the real failure point of a paddle
collar-assembly rings detach individually as hardware fragments
gripWrapHelix rides with gripWrap (explodeWithParent) rather than separating into 11 loose rings
risks: Thickness axis is unobserved: a side view could show the head is thinner or thicker than 16 mm, which would change the three-quarter silhouette but not the front one.

RESOLVED at blockout: the swept edge-guard bead did twist — self_intersection.py found 36% of its sampled vertices inside its own volume — and was rebuilt as an extruded ring. No swept frames remain in the model.
The de-lit albedo still carries residual studio shading (de-light confidence 0.594); under a strong key it can read as double-lit.
Face and rear skins share one material, so the rear inherits the front decal. If the client supplies a rear view this needs a second material, not a texture tweak.

self_intersection.py reports 1-3 inside vertices each on the handle core, grip wrap and butt cap. Those are the lathe/cylinder poles where the profile radius is clamped to 0.0001 at the axis — a numerically degenerate point, not a folded surface. Stated rather than suppressed; re-check if the count ever grows past the pole count.

The two observed repetitions are carried by a single swept component and by material channels, so neither has an instanced-geometry fallback. If the grip is ever seen in extreme close-up, the perforations will read as shading rather than holes.
